sentences.zh: 志第三十八 樂二

translations.literal: Treatise 38: Music, Part Two
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 38: Music, Part Two

sentences.zh: ○樂章一

translations.literal: ○ Music Section One
translations.idiomatic: Music Section One

sentences.zh: 洪武元年圜丘樂章。

translations.literal: Music for the Circular Mound Altar, first year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Hymns for the Circular Mound Altar, Hongwu reign year 1.

sentences.zh: 迎神，《中和之曲》：昊天蒼兮穹窿，廣覆燾兮龐洪。

translations.literal: Welcoming the Spirit, "Moderation and Harmony": azure is the vast Heaven, broadly covering and nurturing in mighty abundance.
translations.idiomatic: Welcoming the Spirit — "Moderation and Harmony": Heaven stands azure and vaulted, spreading its nurture in boundless might.

sentences.zh: 建圜丘兮國之陽，合衆神兮來臨之同。

translations.literal: We have built the Circular Mound at the nation's sunny side; all spirits assemble and come together as one.
translations.idiomatic: On the bright southern flank of the realm we raise the Circular Mound; every spirit gathers and draws near as one.

sentences.zh: 念螻蟻兮微衷，莫自期兮感通。

translations.literal: Thinking of the ant's tiny sincerity, we dare not expect by ourselves to achieve sympathetic communion.
translations.idiomatic: We who are no more than ants in devotion dare not presume that communion will come of its own.

sentences.zh: 思神來兮金玉其容，馭龍鸞兮乘雲駕風。

translations.literal: We think of the spirit coming with jade-and-gold countenance, driving dragon and phoenix, riding cloud and harnessing wind.
translations.idiomatic: We picture the spirit arriving in splendor like jade and gold, guiding dragon and phoenix, borne on cloud and wind.

sentences.zh: 顧南郊兮昭格，望至尊兮崇崇。

translations.literal: We look toward the southern suburb for manifest presence; we gaze upon the supreme sovereign in towering majesty.
translations.idiomatic: We turn to the southern suburb for a clear descent; we behold the supreme sovereign in towering glory.

sentences.zh: 奠玉帛，《肅和之曲》：聖靈皇皇，敬瞻威光。

translations.literal: Offering jade and silk, "Reverent Harmony": the holy spirit is august; we reverently behold its awesome radiance.
translations.idiomatic: Offering jade and silk — "Reverent Harmony": the holy spirit reigns in splendor; in awe we behold its radiant power.

sentences.zh: 玉帛以登，承筐是將。

translations.literal: With jade and silk we ascend; bearing the basket we present them.
translations.idiomatic: Jade and silk are raised on high; in baskets we bear them forward.

sentences.zh: 穆穆崇嚴，神妙難量。

translations.literal: Solemn and lofty in dignity, the spirit's wonder cannot be measured.
translations.idiomatic: Solemn and sublime beyond measure, the spirit's mystery defies reckoning.

sentences.zh: 謹茲禮祭，功徵是皇。

translations.literal: We reverently perform this ritual sacrifice; may merit and auspicious signs be made manifest.
translations.idiomatic: With care we perform this rite of sacrifice; may merit and blessing be made manifest.

sentences.zh: 進俎，《凝和之曲》：祀儀祗陳，物不於大。

translations.literal: Presenting the sacrifice tray, "Concentrated Harmony": the sacrificial rite is reverently set forth; offerings are not made excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Presenting the sacrifice tray — "Concentrated Harmony": the rite is laid out in reverence; nothing is offered beyond what is fitting.

sentences.zh: 敢用純犢，告於覆載。

translations.literal: We dare use a pure calf and announce it to Heaven that covers and Earth that bears.
translations.idiomatic: We dare offer a pure calf and proclaim it to Heaven above and Earth below.

sentences.zh: 惟茲菲薦，恐未周完。

translations.literal: Only this meager offering — we fear it is not yet complete in every respect.
translations.idiomatic: This humble offering alone — we fear it may not yet be wholly sufficient.

sentences.zh: 神其容之，以享以觀。

translations.literal: May the spirit accept it, partake and regard it.
translations.idiomatic: May the spirit deign to accept it, to enjoy and to behold.

sentences.zh: 初獻，《壽和之曲》：眇眇微躬，何敢請於九重，以煩帝聰。

translations.literal: First offering, "Longevity and Harmony": tiny and slight is this humble person; how dare we petition the Ninefold Heights and trouble the Emperor's hearing?
translations.idiomatic: First offering — "Longevity and Harmony": how slight is this humble frame — who dares petition the Ninefold Heights and trouble the Emperor's ear?

sentences.zh: 帝心矜兮，有感而通。

translations.literal: The Emperor's heart is compassionate; there is feeling and communion is achieved.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's heart is merciful; feeling stirs and communion is won.

sentences.zh: 既俯臨於几筵，神繽紛而景從。

translations.literal: Having bowed before the spirit table, the spirits throng in multitudes and follow like shadows.
translations.idiomatic: Having bowed before the spirit table, the spirits gather in throngs and follow like shining shadows.

sentences.zh: 臣雖愚蒙，鼓舞歡容，乃子孫之親祖宗。

translations.literal: Though we ministers are foolish and ignorant, we drum and dance with joyful countenance — such is descendants drawing near to ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Though we ministers are dull and unlearned, we drum and dance with joy — for such is how descendants draw near to their forebears.

sentences.zh: 酌清酒兮在鍾，仰至德兮玄功。

translations.literal: We pour clear wine in the bell-goblet; we look up to supreme virtue and mysterious merit.
translations.idiomatic: We pour clear wine into the bell-goblet; we look up to supreme virtue and its hidden power.

sentences.zh: 亞獻，《豫和之曲》：荷天之寵，眷駐紫壇。

translations.literal: Second offering, "Ease and Harmony": we bear Heaven's favor; graciously stationed at the purple altar.
translations.idiomatic: Second offering — "Ease and Harmony": we bear Heaven's grace, dwelling at the purple altar in favor.

sentences.zh: 中情彌喜，臣庶均懽。

translations.literal: In our inner hearts joy grows ever fuller; ministers and commoners alike rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: Joy wells ever deeper within; ministers and people rejoice as one.

sentences.zh: 趨蹌奉承，我心則寬。

translations.literal: Hastening forward in orderly steps to serve and receive, our hearts are thereby eased.
translations.idiomatic: We hurry forward in measured steps to serve and receive, and our hearts are eased.

sentences.zh: 再獻御前，式燕且安。

translations.literal: We offer again before the sovereign; a feast is held and all is at peace.
translations.idiomatic: We offer again before the throne; the feast proceeds and all is at peace.

sentences.zh: 終獻，《熙和之曲》：小子於茲，惟父天之思，惟恃天之慈，內外殷勤。

translations.literal: Final offering, "Radiant Harmony": here is the young son; he thinks only of the Father Heaven, relies only on Heaven's compassion, diligent within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Final offering — "Radiant Harmony": here stands the young son, mindful only of Father Heaven, trusting only in Heaven's mercy, earnest within and without.

sentences.zh: 何以將之？

translations.literal: With what shall we present offerings?
translations.idiomatic: With what shall we make our offering?

sentences.zh: 奠有芳齊，設有明粢。

translations.literal: We set forth fragrant seasoned offerings; we arrange bright grain sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: We set forth fragrant seasoned dishes and arrange bright grain offerings.

sentences.zh: 喜極而抃，奉神燕娭。

translations.literal: Joy reaches its height and we clap our hands; we present to the spirit a feast of repose.
translations.idiomatic: Joy overflows and we clap our hands; we offer the spirit a feast of delight.

sentences.zh: 禮雖止於三獻，情悠長兮遠而。

translations.literal: Though the rite ends at three offerings, feeling is long and stretches far away.
translations.idiomatic: Though the rite ends with the third offering, devotion lingers long and reaches far.

sentences.zh: 徹饌，《雍和之曲》：烹飪既陳，薦獻斯就。

translations.literal: Removing the feast, "Harmonious Peace": cooking is already set forth; the presentation of offerings is now complete.
translations.idiomatic: Removing the feast — "Harmonious Peace": the cooked offerings stand ready; presentation and sacrifice are complete.

sentences.zh: 神之在位，既歆既右。

translations.literal: The spirit is in its place; it has already enjoyed and already blessed.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit holds its place; it has accepted the offering and granted its blessing.

sentences.zh: 羣臣駿奔，徹茲俎豆。

translations.literal: All ministers gallop forward; we remove these trays and vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers hurry forward and withdraw the trays and vessels.

sentences.zh: 物倘未充，尚幸神宥。

translations.literal: If the offerings are perhaps not yet sufficient, we still hope the spirit will pardon.
translations.idiomatic: If our offerings are not yet fully adequate, we still trust the spirit will forgive.

sentences.zh: 送神，《安和之曲》：神之去兮難延，想遐袂兮翩翩。

translations.literal: Sending off the Spirit, "Secure Harmony": the spirit departs and is hard to detain; we think of distant sleeves fluttering gracefully.
translations.idiomatic: Sending off the Spirit — "Secure Harmony": the spirit departs and cannot be held; we picture distant sleeves fluttering on the wind.

sentences.zh: 萬靈從兮後先，衛神駕兮迴旋。

translations.literal: Myriad spirits follow fore and aft; they guard the spirit's carriage and wheel about.
translations.idiomatic: Myriad spirits follow before and behind, guarding the spirit's carriage as it wheels about.

sentences.zh: 稽首兮瞻天，雲之衢兮眇然。

translations.literal: We bow our heads and gaze toward Heaven; the cloud-path stretches dim and far.
translations.idiomatic: We bow our heads and look toward Heaven; the cloud-road fades into the distance.

sentences.zh: 望燎，《時和之曲》：焚燎於壇，燦爛晶熒。

translations.literal: Gazing at the burning, "Timely Harmony": we burn offerings on the altar; they blaze bright and glittering.
translations.idiomatic: Gazing at the burning — "Timely Harmony": offerings blaze upon the altar, brilliant and gleaming.

sentences.zh: 幣帛牲黍，冀徹帝京。

translations.literal: Silks, silks, sacrificial animals, and millet — we hope they reach the Emperor's capital.
translations.idiomatic: Silks, victims, and grain — we hope they ascend to the celestial court.

sentences.zh: 奉神於陽，昭祀有成。

translations.literal: We receive the spirit in the yang realm; the bright sacrifice is accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: We welcome the spirit in the realm of light; the bright rite is fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 肅然望之，玉宇光明。

translations.literal: Solemnly we gaze upon it; the jade firmament is luminous.
translations.idiomatic: In solemn awe we behold it; the jade heavens shine with light.

sentences.zh: 洪武八年御製圜丘樂章。

translations.literal: Music for the Circular Mound Altar, imperially composed, eighth year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Hymns for the Circular Mound Altar, composed by the emperor, Hongwu reign year 8.

sentences.zh: 迎神：仰惟兮昊穹，臣率百職兮迓迎。

translations.literal: Welcoming the Spirit: looking up to the vast azure vault, the minister leads the hundred offices to greet and welcome.
translations.idiomatic: Welcoming the Spirit: gazing up at the vast heavens, the minister leads every office to greet the descent.

sentences.zh: 幸來臨兮壇中，上下護衛兮景從。

translations.literal: Fortunate is Your coming to the altar's midst; above and below guard and escort, shadows following.
translations.idiomatic: Blessed is Your arrival at the altar's heart; guardians above and below follow like shining shadows.

sentences.zh: 旌幢繚繞兮四維，重悅聖心兮民獲年豐。

translations.literal: Banners and pennants twine about the four quarters; doubly pleasing the sage heart, the people gain bountiful years.
translations.idiomatic: Banners and pennants wind through the four quarters; the sage heart is doubly pleased, and the people reap abundant harvests.

sentences.zh: 奠玉帛：民依時兮用工，感帝德兮大化成功。

translations.literal: Offering jade and silk: the people follow the seasons in their labor; feeling the Emperor's virtue, the great transformation succeeds.
translations.idiomatic: Offering jade and silk: the people labor in season; moved by the Emperor's virtue, the great transformation is achieved.

sentences.zh: 臣將兮以奠，望納兮微衷。

translations.literal: The minister is about to present the offering; we hope it will be received — our humble sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: The minister prepares to present the offering, hoping it will be received — our humble sincerity.

sentences.zh: 進俎：庖人兮列鼎，餚羞兮以成。

translations.literal: Presenting the sacrifice tray: the cook arranges the tripods; delicacies and viands are thereby completed.
translations.idiomatic: Presenting the sacrifice tray: the cooks set out the tripods; delicacies and viands are made ready.

sentences.zh: 方俎兮再獻，願享兮以歆。

translations.literal: The square tray is presented again; we wish You to enjoy and accept.
translations.idiomatic: The square tray is offered once more; we pray You will partake and accept.

sentences.zh: 初獻：靈兮皇皇，穆嚴兮金牀。

translations.literal: First offering: the spirit is august and splendid; solemn and dignified upon the golden couch.
translations.idiomatic: First offering: the spirit reigns in splendor, solemn and dignified upon the golden couch.

sentences.zh: 臣令樂舞兮景張，酒行初獻兮捧觴。

translations.literal: The minister orders music and dance to spread like shadows; wine proceeds in the first offering as we raise the goblet.
translations.idiomatic: The minister orders music and dance to unfold; wine is poured for the first offering as we raise the goblet.

sentences.zh: 亞獻：載斟兮再將，百辟陪祀兮具張。

translations.literal: Second offering: we pour again and present once more; the hundred lords attend the sacrifice, all arrayed.
translations.idiomatic: Second offering: we pour again and present once more; the hundred lords attend the sacrifice, all in place.

sentences.zh: 感聖情兮無已，拜手稽首兮願享。

translations.literal: Feeling the sage feeling without end, we bow with hands joined and heads to the ground, wishing You to enjoy.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by the sage heart without end, we bow with joined hands and bowed heads, praying You will accept.

sentences.zh: 終獻：三獻兮樂舞揚，餚羞具納兮氣藹而芳。

translations.literal: Final offering: three offerings — music and dance rise up; delicacies all presented — vapor misty and fragrant.
translations.idiomatic: Final offering: with the third presentation music and dance ascend; every delicacy is offered, and fragrance fills the air.

sentences.zh: 光朗朗兮上方，況日吉兮時良。

translations.literal: Light shines clear above; moreover the day is auspicious and the hour is good.
translations.idiomatic: Light shines clear on high; moreover the day is auspicious and the hour is propitious.

sentences.zh: 徹饌：粗陳菲薦兮神喜將，感聖心兮何以忘。

translations.literal: Removing the feast: roughly setting forth meager offerings — the spirit is pleased and about to accept; feeling the sage heart — how could we forget?
translations.idiomatic: Removing the feast: though our offerings are humble, the spirit is pleased to accept; touched by the sage heart — how could we ever forget?

sentences.zh: 民福留兮佳氣昂，臣拜手兮謝恩光。

translations.literal: The people's blessing remains; fine vapor rises high; the minister bows with joined hands and thanks the grace of light.
translations.idiomatic: The people's blessing endures and auspicious vapor rises high; the minister bows with joined hands and gives thanks for the radiant grace.

sentences.zh: 送神：旌幢燁燁兮雲衢長，龍車鳳輦兮駕飛揚。

translations.literal: Sending off the Spirit: banners and pennants blaze along the long cloud-road; dragon carriage and phoenix palanquin drive aloft in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Sending off the Spirit: banners blaze along the long cloud-road; dragon carriage and phoenix palanquin soar on high.

sentences.zh: 遙瞻冉冉兮去上方，可見烝民兮永康。

translations.literal: Gazing from afar as You slowly depart for the heights above, we can see the multitude of people in lasting peace.
translations.idiomatic: We watch from afar as You slowly ascend on high, and see the people dwelling in lasting peace.

sentences.zh: 望燎：進羅列兮詣燎方，炬焰發兮煌煌。

translations.literal: Gazing at the burning: advancing in array we proceed to the burning place; torch-flames burst forth, blazing bright.
translations.idiomatic: Gazing at the burning: we advance in ordered ranks to the burning place; torch-flames leap forth, blazing bright.

sentences.zh: 神變化兮物全於上，感至恩兮無量。

translations.literal: The spirit transforms; things are made whole above; feeling supreme grace — it is without measure.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit transforms and offerings are made whole on high; we feel supreme grace beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 洪武二年方丘樂章。

translations.literal: Music for the Square Mound Altar, second year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Hymns for the Square Mound Altar, Hongwu reign year 2.

sentences.zh: 迎神，《中和之曲》：坤德博厚，物資以生。

translations.literal: Welcoming the Spirit, "Moderation and Harmony": Earth's virtue is broad and thick; all things receive from it their life.
translations.idiomatic: Welcoming the Spirit — "Moderation and Harmony": Earth's virtue is vast and deep; all things draw life from it.

sentences.zh: 承天時行，光大且寧。

translations.literal: Receiving Heaven's seasons it acts; its radiance is great and it is tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: It moves in accord with Heaven's seasons, shining great and serene.

sentences.zh: 穆穆皇祇，功化順成。

translations.literal: Solemn is the august Earth Spirit; merit and transformation proceed in harmonious completion.
translations.idiomatic: Solemn is the august Earth Spirit; its transforming work proceeds in perfect order.

sentences.zh: 來御方丘，嚴恭奉迎。

translations.literal: Come to preside at the Square Mound; with stern reverence we welcome You.
translations.idiomatic: Come to preside at the Square Mound; with solemn reverence we welcome You.

sentences.zh: 奠玉帛，《肅和之曲》：地有四維，大琮以方；

translations.literal: Offering jade and silk, "Reverent Harmony": Earth has its four dimensions; the great jade cube is square;
translations.idiomatic: Offering jade and silk — "Reverent Harmony": Earth has its four bounds; the great jade cube is square;

sentences.zh: 土有正色，制幣以黃。

translations.literal: soil has its proper color — ritual silks are fashioned in yellow.
translations.idiomatic: earth has its proper hue, and ritual silks are fashioned in yellow.

sentences.zh: 敬存於中，是薦是將。

translations.literal: Reverence is kept within; thus we offer, thus we present.
translations.idiomatic: Reverence is held within; thus we offer and present.

sentences.zh: 奠之几筵，臨鑑洋洋。

translations.literal: We set them on the spirit table; You look down in vast abundance.
translations.idiomatic: We set them on the spirit table; You look down in boundless grace.

sentences.zh: 進俎，《凝和之曲》：奉將純牡，其牡童犢。

translations.literal: Presenting the sacrifice tray, "Concentrated Harmony": we present a pure bull; the bull is a young calf.
translations.idiomatic: Presenting the sacrifice tray — "Concentrated Harmony": we offer a pure bull, a bull still young.

sentences.zh: 烹飪既嚴，登俎惟肅。

translations.literal: Cooking is already strict and complete; ascending the tray is only with solemnity.
translations.idiomatic: Cooking is performed with utmost care; what ascends the tray is offered in solemn reverence.

sentences.zh: 升壇昭薦，神光下燭。

translations.literal: Ascending the altar in bright presentation; divine light shines down upon it.
translations.idiomatic: We ascend the altar in bright offering; divine light shines down upon it.

sentences.zh: 眷佑邦家，報效惟篤。

translations.literal: Favoring and protecting the state and clan, our repayment of merit is only earnest.
translations.idiomatic: You favor and protect the realm; our repayment is offered in deepest earnest.

sentences.zh: 初獻，《壽和之曲》：午爲盛陽，陰德初萌。

translations.literal: First offering, "Longevity and Harmony": noon is the flourishing yang; yin virtue first sprouts.
translations.idiomatic: First offering — "Longevity and Harmony": noon is the height of yang; yin virtue first stirs.

sentences.zh: 天地相遇，品物光榮。

translations.literal: Heaven and Earth meet; all kinds of things are bright and glorious.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and Earth meet; every kind of thing shines with glory.

sentences.zh: 吉日令辰，明祀攸行。

translations.literal: An auspicious day, a fine hour — the bright sacrifice is thereby conducted.
translations.idiomatic: On an auspicious day, at a propitious hour, the bright sacrifice proceeds.

sentences.zh: 進以醇醴，展其潔清。

translations.literal: We advance with rich wine and unfold its purity and clarity.
translations.idiomatic: We offer rich wine and display its purity and clarity.

sentences.zh: 亞獻，《豫和之曲》：至廣無邊，道全持載。

translations.literal: Second offering, "Ease and Harmony": utmost breadth without boundary; the Way is complete in bearing and sustaining.
translations.idiomatic: Second offering — "Ease and Harmony": boundless in breadth, the Way wholly sustains and bears all.

sentences.zh: 山嶽所憑，海瀆鹹賴。

translations.literal: Mountains and peaks rely upon it; seas and streams all depend upon it.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains and peaks rest upon it; seas and streams all depend upon it.

sentences.zh: 民次水土，既安且泰。

translations.literal: The people follow water and soil; they are already secure and at peace.
translations.idiomatic: The people settle upon water and soil, secure and at peace.

sentences.zh: 酌酒揭虔，功德惟大。

translations.literal: We pour wine and display reverence; merit and virtue are only great.
translations.idiomatic: We pour wine and show our reverence; merit and virtue are surpassingly great.

sentences.zh: 終獻，《熙和之曲》：庸眇之資，有此疆宇。

translations.literal: Final offering, "Radiant Harmony": a mediocre and slight endowment — yet we have this realm and territory.
translations.idiomatic: Final offering — "Radiant Harmony": humble and slight as we are, we yet hold this realm and territory.

sentences.zh: 匪臣攸能，仰承佑助。

translations.literal: It is not what ministers can accomplish; we look up and receive protective aid.
translations.idiomatic: This is no achievement of ministers alone; we look up and receive Your sustaining aid.

sentences.zh: 恩崇父母，臣歡鼓舞。

translations.literal: Grace exalts the parents; ministers rejoice in drumming and dancing.
translations.idiomatic: Grace honors our forebears; the ministers rejoice in drum and dance.

sentences.zh: 八音宣揚，疊侑明醑。

translations.literal: The eight sounds are proclaimed and spread; layered assists of bright wine.
translations.idiomatic: The eight tones resound; bright wine is offered again and again.

sentences.zh: 徹饌，《雍和之曲》：牲牷在俎，籩豆有實。

translations.literal: Removing the feast, "Harmonious Peace": sacrificial animals are on the tray; baskets and vessels have their fullness.
translations.idiomatic: Removing the feast — "Harmonious Peace": sacrificial beasts rest on the tray; baskets and vessels are full.

sentences.zh: 臨之蕣蠁，匪惟飲食。

translations.literal: You preside over them like hibiscus blooms — it is not only food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: You preside over them as over fleeting blooms — this is not food and drink alone.

sentences.zh: 登歌乃徹，薦獻爰畢。

translations.literal: Ascending song is now withdrawn; presentation and offering are hereby completed.
translations.idiomatic: The ascending song is withdrawn; presentation and offering are complete.

sentences.zh: 執事奉承，一其嚴粟。

translations.literal: Those who perform the rites receive and serve, making one their stern reverence.
translations.idiomatic: The attendants receive and serve, united in solemn reverence.

sentences.zh: 送神，《安和之曲》：神化無方，妙用難量。

translations.literal: Sending off the Spirit, "Secure Harmony": spirit transformation has no fixed direction; subtle use is hard to measure.
translations.idiomatic: Sending off the Spirit — "Secure Harmony": the spirit's transformation knows no bounds; its subtle power defies measure.

sentences.zh: 其功顯融，其禮攸長。

translations.literal: Its merit is manifest and harmonious; its rite is thereby long-lasting.
translations.idiomatic: Its merit shines forth in harmony; its rite endures through the ages.

sentences.zh: 飈輪雲旋，龍探鸞翔。

translations.literal: Whirlwind wheels and clouds revolve; dragon probes and phoenix soars.
translations.idiomatic: Whirlwind wheels and clouds revolve; dragon and phoenix soar on high.

sentences.zh: 拜送稽首，瞻禮餘光。

translations.literal: We bow in sending off, heads to the ground; we gaze in ritual upon the remaining radiance.
translations.idiomatic: We bow our heads in farewell and gaze upon the lingering radiance.

sentences.zh: 望瘞，《時和之曲》：牲醴制幣，餕饌惟馨。

translations.literal: Gazing at the burial, "Timely Harmony": sacrificial animals, rich wine, fashioned silks — the spirit-food is only fragrant.
translations.idiomatic: Gazing at the burial — "Timely Harmony": victims, rich wine, and fashioned silks — the spirit-food is fragrant alone.

sentences.zh: 瘞之於坎，以達坤靈。

translations.literal: We bury them in the pit to reach the Earth Spirit.
translations.idiomatic: We bury them in the pit to reach the spirit of Earth.

sentences.zh: 奉神於陰，典禮是程。

translations.literal: We receive the spirit in the yin realm; the canonical rite is thereby fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: We welcome the spirit in the realm of shade; the canonical rite is fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 企而望之，厚壤寬平。

translations.literal: Standing on tiptoe we gaze upon it; the thick soil is broad and level.
translations.idiomatic: We stand and gaze upon it; the deep earth lies broad and level.

sentences.zh: 洪武八年御製方丘樂章。

translations.literal: Music for the Square Mound Altar, imperially composed, eighth year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Hymns for the Square Mound Altar, composed by the emperor, Hongwu reign year 8.

sentences.zh: 迎神：仰皇祇兮駕來，川嶽從迎兮威靈備開，香菸繚繞兮神臨御街。

translations.literal: Welcoming the Spirit: looking up to the august Earth Spirit as You drive to come; rivers and peaks follow to welcome — awesome spirit fully deployed; incense smoke winds about as the spirit arrives at the imperial street.
translations.idiomatic: Welcoming the Spirit: we look up as the august Earth Spirit draws near; rivers and peaks follow to welcome, its awesome presence fully revealed; incense smoke curls as the spirit arrives along the imperial way.

sentences.zh: 漸升壇兮穆穆，靄瑞氣兮應結樓臺。

translations.literal: Gradually ascending the altar, solemn and still; misty auspicious vapor responds and gathers upon towers and terraces.
translations.idiomatic: Step by step we ascend the altar in solemn stillness; auspicious vapor gathers as if towers and terraces were taking form.

sentences.zh: 以微衷兮率職，幸望聖悅兮心諧。

translations.literal: With humble sincerity we lead our duties; we are fortunate to hope for sage pleasure and hearts in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: With humble sincerity we perform our duties, hoping the sage heart is pleased and our hearts are at one.

sentences.zh: 但允臣兮固請，願嘉烝民兮永懷。

translations.literal: Only grant the minister to firmly petition; we wish blessing for the multitude of people in lasting remembrance.
translations.idiomatic: Grant your minister leave to plead earnestly; may the people be blessed and ever held in favor.

sentences.zh: 奠玉帛：臣奉兮以筐，玉帛是進兮歲奠以常。

translations.literal: Offering jade and silk: the minister presents them in baskets; jade and silk are advanced as the yearly offering in constant practice.
translations.idiomatic: Offering jade and silk: the minister bears them in baskets; jade and silk are presented as the yearly offering, ever as custom requires.

sentences.zh: 百辟陪祀兮珮聲琅琅。

translations.literal: The hundred lords attend the sacrifice; pendant sounds ring clear.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred lords attend the sacrifice, their pendants chiming clear.

sentences.zh: 惟南薰兮解慍，映燎炎兮煌煌。

translations.literal: Only the southern breeze dispels irritation; reflected against the blazing fire, all is blazing bright.
translations.idiomatic: The southern breeze alone dispels all vexation; against the blazing fire all shines resplendent.

sentences.zh: 進俎：庖人兮淨湯，大烹牲兮氣靄而芳。

translations.literal: Presenting the sacrifice tray: the cook purifies the broth; great cooking of victims — vapor misty and fragrant.
translations.idiomatic: Presenting the sacrifice tray: the cooks prepare pure broth; the great victims are cooked, and fragrance fills the air.

sentences.zh: 以微衷兮獻上，曰享兮曰康。

translations.literal: With humble sincerity we present upward, saying "Enjoy" and saying "Peace."
translations.idiomatic: With humble sincerity we offer them up, praying enjoyment and peace.

sentences.zh: 初獻：初獻行兮捧觴，聖靈穆穆兮洋洋。

translations.literal: First offering: the first offering proceeds as we raise the goblet; the holy spirit is solemn, vast and abundant.
translations.idiomatic: First offering: the first offering proceeds as we raise the goblet; the holy spirit reigns solemn and vast.

sentences.zh: 爲烝民兮永康，鑑豐年兮耿光。

translations.literal: For the multitude of people in lasting peace; discerning abundant years in bright radiance.
translations.idiomatic: For the people in lasting peace; discerning abundant harvests in shining light.

sentences.zh: 亞獻：雜餚羞兮已張，法前王兮典章。

translations.literal: Second offering: assorted delicacies and viands are already spread; following the former kings' canonical regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Second offering: assorted delicacies are already set out, following the canonical regulations of former kings.

sentences.zh: 臣固展兮情悃，用斟醴兮載觴。

translations.literal: The minister firmly displays sincere feeling; using poured rich wine we bear the goblet.
translations.idiomatic: The minister earnestly shows his sincere heart, pouring rich wine and bearing the goblet.

sentences.zh: 終獻：爵三獻兮禮將終，臣心眷戀兮無窮。

translations.literal: Final offering: the three offerings — the rite is about to end; the minister's heart is attached in love without end.
translations.idiomatic: Final offering: with the third cup the rite draws near its end; the minister's heart clings in devotion without end.

sentences.zh: 恐餚羞兮未具，將何報兮神功。

translations.literal: We fear the delicacies are not yet complete; with what shall we repay the divine merit?
translations.idiomatic: We fear the delicacies are not yet complete — how shall we repay divine merit?

sentences.zh: 徹饌：俎豆徹兮神熙，鸞輿駕兮旋歸。

translations.literal: Removing the feast: trays and vessels are withdrawn — the spirit is pleased; the phoenix carriage is harnessed and wheels about to return.
translations.idiomatic: Removing the feast: trays and vessels are withdrawn, the spirit pleased; the phoenix carriage is harnessed and turns homeward.

sentences.zh: 百神翼翼兮雲衣。

translations.literal: The hundred spirits wing closely in cloud-garments.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred spirits hover close in garments of cloud.

sentences.zh: 敬奉行兮弗敢違。

translations.literal: Reverently we perform and follow — we dare not disobey.
translations.idiomatic: We perform and follow in reverence, daring not to disobey.

sentences.zh: 送神：祥風興兮悠悠，雲衢開兮民福留。

translations.literal: Sending off the Spirit: auspicious wind rises, long and lingering; the cloud-road opens and the people's blessing remains.
translations.idiomatic: Sending off the Spirit: auspicious wind rises, long and lingering; the cloud-road opens and the people's blessing endures.

sentences.zh: 歲樂烝民兮大有，想洋洋兮舉觴載酒。

translations.literal: Year by year the multitude rejoice in great abundance; we think of vast abundance — raising goblets and bearing wine.
translations.idiomatic: Year by year the people rejoice in great abundance; we picture vast joy — raising goblets and bearing wine.

sentences.zh: 望瘞：餚羞玉帛兮瘞坎中，遙瞻隱隱兮龍旗從。

translations.literal: Gazing at the burial: delicacies, jade, and silk are buried in the pit; gazing from afar, dimly visible — the dragon banners follow.
translations.idiomatic: Gazing at the burial: delicacies, jade, and silk are buried in the pit; gazing from afar we see the dragon banners following, dimly visible.

sentences.zh: 祀事成兮盡微衷，感厚德兮民福雍雍。

translations.literal: The sacrificial affair is accomplished — we exhaust our humble sincerity; feeling thick virtue, the people's blessing is harmonious and abundant.
translations.idiomatic: The sacrifice is complete and our humble sincerity is spent; moved by deep virtue, the people's blessing flows in harmony.

sentences.zh: 洪武十二年合祀天地樂章。

translations.literal: Music for the joint sacrifice to Heaven and Earth, twelfth year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Hymns for the joint sacrifice to Heaven and Earth, Hongwu reign year 12.

sentences.zh: 迎神，《中和之曲》：荷蒙天地兮君主華夷，欽承踊躍兮備筵而祭，誠惶無已兮寸衷微，仰瞻俯首兮惟願來期。

translations.literal: Welcoming the Spirit, "Moderation and Harmony": we bear Heaven and Earth's grace as sovereign over Chinese and barbarians; reverently receiving, we leap and spring to prepare the feast and sacrifice; sincere awe without end — our inch of heart is slight; looking up and bowing our heads, we only wish for the coming appointed time.
translations.idiomatic: Welcoming the Spirit — 《Moderation and Harmony》: graced by Heaven and Earth, sovereign over all within the realm, we reverently leap to prepare the feast and sacrifice; in endless awe our humble hearts are slight; looking up and bowing low, we pray only for the appointed arrival.

sentences.zh: 想龍翔鳳舞兮慶雲飛，必昭昭穆穆兮降壇壝。

translations.literal: We think of dragon soaring and phoenix dancing, auspicious clouds flying; surely in bright splendor and solemn grace You will descend to the altar mound.
translations.idiomatic: We picture dragon and phoenix soaring, auspicious clouds flying; surely in bright splendor and solemn grace You will descend to the altar mound.

sentences.zh: 奠玉帛，《肅和之曲》：天垂風露兮雨澤沾，黃壤氤氳兮氣化全。

translations.literal: Offering jade and silk, "Reverent Harmony": Heaven sends down wind and dew, rain and moisture soaking through; yellow soil is misty and dense, qi transformation complete.
translations.idiomatic: Offering jade and silk — 《Reverent Harmony》: Heaven sends down wind and dew, rain soaking the land; yellow earth is rich with vapor, transformation complete.

sentences.zh: 民勤畝兮束帛鮮，臣當設宴兮奉來前。

translations.literal: The people labor in the fields; bundled silks are fresh; the minister should set the feast and present them coming forward.
translations.idiomatic: The people labor in the fields; bundled silks are fresh; the minister sets the feast and presents them before You.

sentences.zh: 進俎以後，鹹同八年圜丘詞。

translations.literal: After presenting the sacrifice tray, all are the same as the eighth-year Circular Mound lyrics.
translations.idiomatic: From presenting the sacrifice tray onward, the lyrics are the same as those for the Circular Mound in year 8.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖九年復定分祀圜丘樂章。

translations.literal: Music for the Circular Mound Altar, re-fixed for separate sacrifice, ninth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: Hymns for the Circular Mound Altar, re-established for separate sacrifice, Jiajing reign year 9.

sentences.zh: 迎神，《中和之曲》：仰惟玄造兮於皇昊穹，時當肇陽兮大禮欽崇。

translations.literal: Welcoming the Spirit, "Moderation and Harmony": looking up to the mysterious creation, august is the vast azure vault; the season is the beginning of yang — the great rite is reverently honored.
translations.idiomatic: Welcoming the Spirit — 《Moderation and Harmony》: we look up to the mysterious creation, august the vast heavens; at the season when yang first rises, the great rite is reverently honored.

sentences.zh: 臣惟蒲柳兮螻蟻之衷，伏承春命兮職統羣工。

translations.literal: The minister is only like willow or ant in sincerity; prostrate, we receive the spring command and oversee all the offices.
translations.idiomatic: We ministers are frail as willow, slight as ants in heart; bowing low we receive the spring command and oversee every office.

sentences.zh: 深懷愚昧兮恐負洪德，爰遵彝典兮勉竭微衷。

translations.literal: Deeply cherishing our ignorance, we fear failing the vast virtue; thus following the constant canon, we strive to exhaust our slight sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply aware of our ignorance, we fear failing vast virtue; following the ancient canon, we strive to offer our humble utmost.

sentences.zh: 遙瞻天闕兮寶輦臨壇，臣當稽首兮祗迓恩隆。

translations.literal: Gazing from afar at the celestial gate — the precious carriage arrives at the altar; the minister should bow head to ground and reverently welcome the lofty grace.
translations.idiomatic: We gaze from afar at the celestial gate as the precious carriage reaches the altar; we bow our heads to the ground and reverently welcome sublime grace.

sentences.zh: 百辟陪列兮舞拜於前，萬神翊衛兮以西以東。

translations.literal: The hundred lords attend in ranks, dancing and bowing in front; myriad spirits flank and guard, to the west and to the east.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred lords stand in ranks, dancing and bowing before You; myriad spirits guard on every side, west and east.

sentences.zh: 臣俯伏迎兮敬瞻帝御，願垂歆鑑兮拜德曷窮。

translations.literal: The minister prostrates in welcome and reverently gazes upon the Emperor's presence; we wish You would lower acceptance and regard — bowing in virtue, how could it end?
translations.idiomatic: We prostrate ourselves in welcome and gaze upon the imperial presence; we pray You will look down in acceptance — our thanks for grace knows no end.

sentences.zh: 奠玉帛，《肅和之曲》龍輿既降兮奉禮先，爰有束帛兮暨瑤瑄。

translations.literal: Offering jade and silk, "Reverent Harmony": the dragon carriage has already descended — we perform the rite first; thus there are bundled silks and jade bi and square jade.
translations.idiomatic: Offering jade and silk — 《Reverent Harmony》: the dragon carriage has descended and we perform the rite first; bundled silks are here, with jade bi and square jade.

sentences.zh: 臣謹上獻兮進帝前，仰祈聽納兮荷蒼乾。

translations.literal: The minister reverently presents upward before the Emperor; looking up we pray for hearing and acceptance, bearing the azure Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The minister reverently presents them before the Emperor; we pray they will be heard and accepted, bearing Heaven's grace.

sentences.zh: 進俎，《凝和之曲》：餚羞珍饌兮薦上玄，庖人列鼎兮致精虔。

translations.literal: Presenting the sacrifice tray, "Concentrated Harmony": delicacies and precious viands are offered to the Supreme Mystery; cooks arrange tripods and achieve utmost reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Presenting the sacrifice tray — 《Concentrated Harmony》: delicacies and precious viands are offered to the Supreme Mystery; cooks set out the tripods in utmost reverence.

sentences.zh: 臣盍祗獻兮馨醴牷，願垂歆享兮民福淵。

translations.literal: Should not the minister reverently present fragrant wine and sacrificial beasts? We wish You would lower enjoyment — the people's blessing is deep.
translations.idiomatic: How should the minister not reverently offer fragrant wine and victims? We pray You will partake — the people's blessing runs deep.

sentences.zh: 初獻，《壽和之曲》：禮嚴初獻兮奉觴，臣將上進兮聖皇。

translations.literal: First offering, "Longevity and Harmony": the rite is stern in first offering as we bear the goblet; the minister is about to advance upward to the sage sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: First offering — 《Longevity and Harmony》: the rite is solemn as we bear the first goblet; the minister advances it to the sage sovereign.

sentences.zh: 聖皇垂享兮穆穆，臣拜手兮何以忘。

translations.literal: The sage sovereign lowers enjoyment, solemn and still; the minister bows with joined hands — how could we forget?
translations.idiomatic: The sage sovereign partakes in solemn grace; the minister bows with joined hands — how could we ever forget?

sentences.zh: 亞獻，《豫和之曲》：禮觴再舉兮薦玉漿，帝顏歆悅兮民福昂。

translations.literal: Second offering, "Ease and Harmony": the rite's goblet is raised again, presenting jade nectar; the Emperor's countenance is pleased in enjoyment — the people's blessing rises high.
translations.idiomatic: Second offering — 《Ease and Harmony》: the goblet is raised again, presenting jade nectar; the Emperor is pleased in enjoyment and the people's blessing rises high.

sentences.zh: 民生有賴兮感上蒼，臣惟鞠拜兮荷恩長。

translations.literal: The people's life has reliance — we feel the upper azure; the minister only bows deeply, bearing grace long.
translations.idiomatic: The people's lives depend upon Heaven; the minister bows deeply, bearing grace without end.

sentences.zh: 終獻，《熙和之曲》：三獻兮禮告成，一念微衷兮露悃情。

translations.literal: Final offering, "Radiant Harmony": three offerings — the rite announces completion; one thought of humble sincerity reveals sincere feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Final offering — 《Radiant Harmony》: with three offerings the rite announces its completion; one humble thought reveals our sincere hearts.

sentences.zh: 景張樂舞兮響鍠鋐，仰瞻聖容兮俯錫恩泓。

translations.literal: Music and dance spread like shadows, sound clanging and booming; looking up we gaze upon the sage countenance, looking down bestowed grace flows deep.
translations.idiomatic: Music and dance unfold, bells and drums resounding; we gaze up at the sage countenance as grace pours down from on high.

sentences.zh: 徹饌，《雍和之曲》：祀禮竣兮精意禋，三獻備兮誠已申。

translations.literal: Removing the feast, "Harmonious Peace": the sacrificial rite is complete — refined intent in sacrifice; three offerings prepared — sincerity already expressed.
translations.idiomatic: Removing the feast — 《Harmonious Peace》: the sacrificial rite is complete, refined intent fulfilled; three offerings made, sincerity fully expressed.

sentences.zh: 敬徹弗遲兮肅恭寅，恐多弗備兮惟賴洪仁。

translations.literal: Reverently withdrawing without delay, solemn and respectful; fearing much is not yet prepared — we only rely on vast benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: We withdraw reverently without delay, solemn and respectful; fearing our offerings are not enough, we rely only on vast benevolence.

sentences.zh: 送神，《清和之曲》：禋事訖終兮百辟維張，帝垂歆鑑兮沐澤汪洋。

translations.literal: Sending off the Spirit, "Clear Harmony": the sacrificial affair ends — the hundred lords are all arrayed; the Emperor lowers acceptance and regard — bathed in grace, vast as the ocean.
translations.idiomatic: Sending off the Spirit — 《Clear Harmony》: the sacrifice ends and the hundred lords stand arrayed; the Emperor looks down in acceptance and we are bathed in grace vast as the sea.

sentences.zh: 龍車冉冉兮寶駕旋雲，靈風鼓舞兮瑞露清瀼。

translations.literal: The dragon carriage slowly proceeds; the precious ride wheels back through clouds; spirit wind drums and dances; auspicious dew is clear and abundant.
translations.idiomatic: The dragon carriage moves slowly, the precious ride wheeling back through clouds; spirit wind stirs and auspicious dew runs clear.

sentences.zh: 洪恩浩蕩兮無以爲酬，粗陳菲薦兮已感歆嘗。

translations.literal: Vast grace is boundless — there is nothing with which to repay; roughly setting forth meager offerings — we have already felt acceptance and tasting.
translations.idiomatic: Vast grace is boundless and beyond repayment; though our offerings are humble, we have already felt acceptance.

sentences.zh: 香氣騰芳兮上徹帝座，仰瞻聖造兮賜福羣方。

translations.literal: Fragrant vapor rises and ascends to reach the Emperor's seat; looking up we gaze upon the sage creation — bestowing blessing on all regions.
translations.idiomatic: Fragrant vapor rises to the imperial seat; we look up at the sage creation bestowing blessing on every quarter.

sentences.zh: 臣同率土兮載歡載感，祗回寶輦兮鳳嘯龍翔。

translations.literal: The minister together with all within the realm — bearing joy and bearing feeling; reverently the precious carriage returns — phoenix cries and dragon soars.
translations.idiomatic: The minister with all within the realm rejoices and gives thanks; reverently the precious carriage returns, phoenix crying and dragon soaring.

sentences.zh: 誠惶誠恐兮仰戀彌切，願福生民兮永錫亨昌。

translations.literal: Sincere awe, sincere fear — looking up in longing ever more keen; we wish blessing for the living people — forever bestowing prosperity and splendor.
translations.idiomatic: In sincere awe and fear we look up with ever keener longing; we pray blessing for the people, prosperity bestowed forever.

sentences.zh: 望燎，《時和之曲》：龍駕寶輦兮升帝鄉，御羞菲帛兮奉燎方。

translations.literal: Gazing at the burning, "Timely Harmony": dragon carriage and precious ride ascend to the Emperor's realm; imperial delicacies and meager silks are offered at the burning place.
translations.idiomatic: Gazing at the burning — 《Timely Harmony》: dragon carriage and precious ride ascend to the celestial realm; imperial delicacies and silks are offered at the burning place.

sentences.zh: 環珮鏗鏘兮羅壇壝，炬焰特舉兮氣輝煌。

translations.literal: Ring-pendants clang and ring, arrayed about the altar mound; torch-flames are specially raised — vapor blazing bright.
translations.idiomatic: Pendants ring clear around the altar mound; torches are raised high and flame blazes bright.

sentences.zh: 生民蒙福兮聖澤沾，臣荷眷佑兮拜謝恩光。

translations.literal: The living people receive blessing — sage moisture soaks through; the minister bears favoring protection and bows in thanks for grace of light.
translations.idiomatic: The people receive blessing, soaked in sage grace; the minister bears favoring protection and bows in thanks for radiant grace.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖九年復定方丘樂章。

translations.literal: Music for the Square Mound Altar, re-fixed, ninth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: Hymns for the Square Mound Altar, re-established, Jiajing reign year 9.

sentences.zh: 迎神，《中和之曲》：俯瞻兮鳳輦來，靈風兮拂九垓。

translations.literal: Welcoming the Spirit, "Moderation and Harmony": looking down we behold — the phoenix carriage comes; spirit wind brushes the nine realms.
translations.idiomatic: Welcoming the Spirit — 《Moderation and Harmony》: we look down as the phoenix carriage draws near; spirit wind brushes the nine realms.

sentences.zh: 川嶽從兮後先，百辟列兮襄陪。

translations.literal: Rivers and peaks follow fore and aft; the hundred lords are ranked, assisting in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Rivers and peaks follow before and behind; the hundred lords stand in ranks to attend.

sentences.zh: 臣拜首兮迓迎，願臨享兮幸哉。

translations.literal: The minister bows head to ground in greeting and welcome; we wish You would come to enjoy — how fortunate!
translations.idiomatic: The minister bows his head to the ground in welcome; we pray You will come to partake — how blessed!

sentences.zh: 奠玉帛，《廣和之曲》：祀禮有嚴兮奉虔，玉帛在笥兮來前。

translations.literal: Offering jade and silk, "Broad Harmony": the sacrificial rite has sternness — we present in reverence; jade and silk are in the boxes, coming forward.
translations.idiomatic: Offering jade and silk — 《Broad Harmony》: the sacrificial rite is solemn and we present in reverence; jade and silk in their cases are brought forward.

sentences.zh: 皇靈垂享兮以納，烝民率土兮樂豐年。

translations.literal: The august spirit lowers enjoyment and accepts; the multitude of people throughout the realm rejoice in abundant years.
translations.idiomatic: The august spirit deigns to accept; the people throughout the realm rejoice in abundant harvests.

sentences.zh: 進俎，《咸和之曲》：餚羞馨兮氣芳，庖人奉役兮和湯。

translations.literal: Presenting the sacrifice tray, "All Harmony": delicacies are fragrant, vapor aromatic; cooks perform their service and harmonize the broth.
translations.idiomatic: Presenting the sacrifice tray — 《All Harmony》: delicacies are fragrant, the air aromatic; cooks perform their service and prepare the broth.

sentences.zh: 奉進兮皇祗歆慰，臣稽首兮敬將。

translations.literal: Presented and advanced — the august Earth Spirit is pleased and comforted; the minister bows head to ground and reverently presents.
translations.idiomatic: We present them forward — the august Earth Spirit is pleased; the minister bows his head and reverently offers them.

sentences.zh: 初獻，《壽和之曲》：酒行初獻兮樂舞張，齊醴明潔兮氙香。

translations.literal: First offering, "Longevity and Harmony": wine proceeds in first offering — music and dance spread; pure wine is bright and clean, fragrant vapor rising.
translations.idiomatic: First offering — 《Longevity and Harmony》: wine is poured for the first offering, music and dance unfold; pure wine is bright and clean, fragrant vapor rising.

sentences.zh: 願垂享兮以歆，生民安兮永康。

translations.literal: We wish You would lower enjoyment and accept; the living people are secure in lasting peace.
translations.idiomatic: We pray You will deign to partake; the people are secure in lasting peace.

sentences.zh: 亞獻，《安和之曲》：載獻兮奉觴，神顏和懿兮以嘗。

translations.literal: Second offering, "Secure Harmony": bearing the offering we present the goblet; the spirit's countenance is harmonious and kindly as it tastes.
translations.idiomatic: Second offering — 《Secure Harmony》: we bear the offering and present the goblet; the spirit's countenance is gentle and kindly as it tastes.

sentences.zh: 功隆厚載兮配天，民感德兮無量。

translations.literal: Merit is lofty — thick bearing matches Heaven; the people feel virtue without measure.
translations.idiomatic: Merit is lofty — Earth's sustaining power pairs with Heaven; the people feel virtue beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 終獻，《時和之曲》：三進兮玉露清，百職奔繞兮佩環鳴。

translations.literal: Final offering, "Timely Harmony": three advances — jade dew is clear; the hundred offices hurry circling about — pendant rings sound.
translations.idiomatic: Final offering — 《Timely Harmony》: three presentations — jade dew is clear; the hundred offices hurry about, pendants ringing.

sentences.zh: 鳧鍾鷺鼓兮韻錚鍧，願留福兮羣生。

translations.literal: Wild-goose bells and egret drums — rhythm clanging and booming; we wish to leave blessing for all living beings.
translations.idiomatic: Wild-goose bells and egret drums resound; we pray blessing may remain for all living beings.

sentences.zh: 徹饌，《貞和之曲》：禮告終兮徹敢違，深惟一念兮誠意微。

translations.literal: Removing the feast, "Upright Harmony": the rite announces its end — dare we disobey in withdrawing? Deeply considering one thought — sincerity is slight.
translations.idiomatic: Removing the feast — 《Upright Harmony》: the rite announces its end — who would dare delay withdrawal? Deep in one thought we know our sincerity is slight.

sentences.zh: 神垂博容兮聽納，恐未備兮惟慈依。

translations.literal: The spirit lowers broad acceptance and listens to receive; we fear things are not yet complete — we only rely on compassion.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit in broad acceptance listens and receives; fearing our offerings are incomplete, we rely only on compassion.

sentences.zh: 送神，《寧和之曲》：禮成兮誠已伸，駕還兮法從陳。

translations.literal: Sending off the Spirit, "Tranquil Harmony": the rite is accomplished — sincerity already expressed; the carriage returns — the ritual escort is arrayed.
translations.idiomatic: Sending off the Spirit — 《Tranquil Harmony》: the rite is complete and sincerity expressed; the carriage returns, the ritual escort arrayed.

sentences.zh: 靈祇列兮以隨，百辟拜兮恭寅。

translations.literal: Spirit lords are ranked and follow along; the hundred lords bow in respectful reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit lords rank themselves to follow; the hundred lords bow in respectful reverence.

sentences.zh: 望坤宮兮奉辭，願普福兮烝民。

translations.literal: Gazing toward the Earth Palace we present our farewell; we wish universal blessing for the multitude of people.
translations.idiomatic: We gaze toward the Earth Palace and take our leave; we pray universal blessing for all the people.

sentences.zh: 望燎，曲同《寧和》。

translations.literal: Gazing at the burning — the tune is the same as "Tranquil Harmony."
translations.idiomatic: Gazing at the burning — the tune is the same as 《Tranquil Harmony》.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年朝日樂章。

translations.literal: Music for the Morning Sun sacrifice, third year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Hymns for the Morning Sun sacrifice, Hongwu reign year 3.

sentences.zh: 二十一年罷。

translations.literal: Abolished in the twenty-first year.
translations.idiomatic: Abolished in year 21.

sentences.zh: 迎神，《熙和之曲》：吉日良辰，祀典式陳。

translations.literal: Welcoming the Spirit, "Radiant Harmony": an auspicious day, a fine hour — the sacrificial canon is formally set forth.
translations.idiomatic: Welcoming the Spirit — 《Radiant Harmony》: on an auspicious day, at a propitious hour, the sacrificial canon is formally set forth.

sentences.zh: 純陽之精，惟是大明。

translations.literal: The essence of pure yang — only this is great brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: The essence of pure yang — this alone is great brilliance.

sentences.zh: 濯濯厥靈，昭鑑我心。

translations.literal: Bright and clear is its spirit; it brightly mirrors my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Bright and clear is its spirit; it brightly mirrors our hearts.

sentences.zh: 以候以迎，來格來歆。

translations.literal: We wait and we welcome; come near, come and enjoy.
translations.idiomatic: We wait and we welcome; come near, come and accept our offering.

sentences.zh: 奠幣，《保和之曲》：靈旗蒞止，有赫其威。

translations.literal: Offering silks, "Preserving Harmony": the spirit banner arrives and halts; its awesomeness is blazing.
translations.idiomatic: Offering silks — 《Preserving Harmony》: the spirit banner arrives and halts; its power is blazing bright.

sentences.zh: 一念潛通，幽明弗違。

translations.literal: One thought secretly connects; dark and bright do not diverge.
translations.idiomatic: One thought secretly connects; the hidden and the manifest are not divided.

sentences.zh: 有幣在篚，物薄而微。

translations.literal: There are silks in the basket; the things are thin and slight.
translations.idiomatic: Silks rest in the basket, humble and slight.

sentences.zh: 神兮安留，尚其享之。

translations.literal: Spirit, peacefully remain; still partake of them.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit, abide in peace; deign still to accept them.

sentences.zh: 初獻，《安和之曲》：神兮我留，有薦必受。

translations.literal: First offering, "Secure Harmony": Spirit, I remain; whenever there is offering, You must receive.
translations.idiomatic: First offering — 《Secure Harmony》: Spirit, I remain; whenever offering is made, You surely receive.

sentences.zh: 享祀之初，奠茲醴酒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the enjoyment sacrifice, we set forth this rich wine.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the sacrificial feast, we set forth this rich wine.

sentences.zh: 晨光初升，祥徵應候。

translations.literal: Morning light first rises; auspicious signs respond to the season.
translations.idiomatic: Morning light first rises; auspicious signs answer to the season.

sentences.zh: 何以侑觴，樂陳雅奏。

translations.literal: With what shall we assist the goblet? Music is set forth in elegant performance.
translations.idiomatic: With what shall we accompany the goblet? Music is performed in elegant style.

sentences.zh: 亞獻，《中和之曲》：我祀維何？

translations.literal: Second offering, "Moderation and Harmony": what is our sacrifice?
translations.idiomatic: Second offering — 《Moderation and Harmony》: what is our sacrifice?

sentences.zh: 奉茲犧牲，爰酌醴齊，貳觴載升。

translations.literal: We present these sacrificial victims; thus we pour rich wine, the second goblet is borne upward.
translations.idiomatic: We present these sacrificial victims, pour rich wine, and raise the second goblet.

sentences.zh: 洋洋如在，式燕以寧。

translations.literal: Vast and abundant as if present; a feast is held and all is at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Present in vast abundance; a feast is held and all is at peace.

sentences.zh: 庶表微衷，交於神明。

translations.literal: We hope to display humble sincerity, communing with the spirits bright.
translations.idiomatic: We hope to show our humble hearts, communing with the spirits bright.

sentences.zh: 終獻，《肅和之曲》：執事有嚴，品物斯祭，稷非馨，式將其意。

translations.literal: Final offering, "Reverent Harmony": those who perform the rite have sternness; all items are thereby sacrificed; millet is not fragrant — we thereby convey the intent.
translations.idiomatic: Final offering — 《Reverent Harmony》: the attendants are strict; every item is offered in sacrifice; though millet lacks fragrance, we convey our intent.

sentences.zh: 薦茲酒醴，成我常祀。

translations.literal: We present this wine and rich brew, completing our constant sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: We present this wine and rich brew, completing our regular sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 神其顧歆，永言樂只。

translations.literal: May the spirit turn and enjoy; forever speak of joy.
translations.idiomatic: May the spirit look down and accept; may joy endure forever.

sentences.zh: 徹饌，《凝和之曲》：春祈秋報，率爲我民。

translations.literal: Removing the feast, "Concentrated Harmony": spring prayer and autumn thanksgiving — all for our people.
translations.idiomatic: Removing the feast — 《Concentrated Harmony》: spring prayer and autumn thanksgiving — all for our people.

sentences.zh: 我民之生，賴於爾神。

translations.literal: Our people's life depends upon you, spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Our people's lives depend upon you, spirit.

sentences.zh: 維神佑之，康寧是臻。

translations.literal: Only the spirit protects them; peace and security are thereby attained.
translations.idiomatic: Only the spirit protects them; peace and security are thereby attained.

sentences.zh: 祭祀雲畢，神其樂忻。

translations.literal: The sacrifice is like clouds completed; may the spirit rejoice in pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: The sacrifice is now complete; may the spirit rejoice in delight.

sentences.zh: 送神，《壽和之曲》：三獻禮終，九成樂作。

translations.literal: Sending off the Spirit, "Longevity and Harmony": three offerings — the rite ends; the Nine Accomplishments music is performed.
translations.idiomatic: Sending off the Spirit — "Longevity and Harmony": the three offerings are complete and the Nine Accomplishments music is performed.

sentences.zh: 神人以和，既燕且樂。

translations.literal: Spirit and human are in harmony; a feast is already held and there is joy.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit and human are in harmony; the feast proceeds and all rejoice.

sentences.zh: 雲車風馭，靈光昭灼。

translations.literal: Cloud carriage, wind harness; spirit light blazes bright.
translations.idiomatic: Cloud carriage and wind harness; spirit light blazes forth.

sentences.zh: 瞻望以思，邈彼寥廓。

translations.literal: Gazing and looking in thought; far away is that vast expanse.
translations.idiomatic: We gaze and ponder; far away lies the vast expanse.

sentences.zh: 望燎，《豫和之曲》：俎豆既徹，禮樂已終。

translations.literal: Gazing at the burning, "Ease and Harmony": trays and vessels are already withdrawn; ritual and music are already ended.
translations.idiomatic: Gazing at the burning — "Ease and Harmony": trays and vessels are withdrawn; ritual and music have ended.

sentences.zh: 神之雲旋，倏將焉從。

translations.literal: The spirit like clouds wheels about; suddenly — whither will it follow?
translations.idiomatic: The spirit wheels like clouds; suddenly — whither does it go?

sentences.zh: 以望以燎，庶幾感通。

translations.literal: By gazing and by burning, we hope perhaps for sympathetic communion.
translations.idiomatic: By gazing and burning we hope for sympathetic communion.

sentences.zh: 時和歲豐，維神之功。

translations.literal: Seasons harmonious, years abundant — only the spirit's merit.
translations.idiomatic: Seasons in harmony, years abundant — this is the spirit's work alone.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖九年復定朝日樂章。

translations.literal: Music for the Morning Sun sacrifice, re-fixed, ninth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: Hymns for the Morning Sun sacrifice, re-established, Jiajing reign year 9.

sentences.zh: 迎神，《熙和之曲》：仰瞻兮大明，位奠兮王宮。

translations.literal: Welcoming the Spirit, "Radiant Harmony": looking up we behold great brilliance; the position is set at the royal palace.
translations.idiomatic: Welcoming the Spirit — "Radiant Harmony": we look up at great brilliance, the rite set at the royal palace.

sentences.zh: 時當仲春兮氣融，爰遵祀禮兮報功。

translations.literal: The season is mid-spring — vapor merges; thus following sacrificial rite we repay merit.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-spring has come and the air is mild; we follow the sacrificial rite to repay merit.

sentences.zh: 微誠兮祈神昭鑑，願來享兮迓神聰。

translations.literal: Slight sincerity — we pray the spirit brightly mirrors; we wish You would come to enjoy and welcome the spirit's hearing.
translations.idiomatic: With humble sincerity we pray the spirit will look down; we wish You would come and accept our welcome.

sentences.zh: 奠玉帛，《凝和之曲》：神靈壇兮肅其恭，有帛在篚兮赤琮。

translations.literal: Offering jade and silk, "Concentrated Harmony": the spirit altar — solemn is the reverence; there is silk in the basket and a red jade cube.
translations.idiomatic: Offering jade and silk — "Concentrated Harmony": at the spirit altar all is solemn; silk rests in the basket with a red jade cube.

sentences.zh: 奉神兮祈享以納，予躬奠兮忻以顒。

translations.literal: We present to the spirit and pray enjoyment be accepted; I myself set forth the offering, joyful and uplifted.
translations.idiomatic: We present to the spirit and pray acceptance; I myself set forth the offering, joyful and uplifted.

sentences.zh: 初獻，《壽和之曲》：玉帛方奠兮神歆，酒行初獻兮舞呈。

translations.literal: First offering, "Longevity and Harmony": jade and silk are just set forth — the spirit enjoys; wine proceeds in first offering — dance is presented.
translations.idiomatic: First offering — "Longevity and Harmony": jade and silk are set forth and the spirit accepts; wine is poured for the first offering and dance is presented.

sentences.zh: 齊芳馨兮犧色騂，神容悅兮鑑予情。

translations.literal: Together fragrant and fine — sacrificial color is chestnut; the spirit's countenance is pleased and mirrors my feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Fragrant offerings together, victims chestnut-red; the spirit is pleased and regards our hearts.

sentences.zh: 亞獻，《時和之曲》：二齊升兮氣芬芳，神顏怡和兮喜將。

translations.literal: Second offering, "Timely Harmony": two seasoned offerings rise — vapor fragrant; the spirit's face is harmonious and kindly, joy about to come.
translations.idiomatic: Second offering — "Timely Harmony": two offerings rise, fragrance in the air; the spirit's face is gentle and joy draws near.

sentences.zh: 予令樂舞兮具張，願垂普照兮民康。

translations.literal: I order music and dance fully spread; we wish You would lower universal shining — the people secure.
translations.idiomatic: I order music and dance to unfold; we pray Your light will shine on all and the people be secure.

sentences.zh: 終獻，《保和之曲》：殷勤三獻兮告成，羣職在列兮周盈。

translations.literal: Final offering, "Preserving Harmony": earnest three offerings announce completion; all offices are ranked in the circle, full.
translations.idiomatic: Final offering — "Preserving Harmony": with earnest third offering we announce completion; every office stands in ranks, the circle full.

sentences.zh: 神錫休兮福民生，萬世永賴兮神功明。

translations.literal: The spirit bestows rest — blessing the people's life; ten thousand ages forever rely — divine merit is bright.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit bestows blessing on the people's lives; for ten thousand ages we rely on bright divine merit.

sentences.zh: 徹饌，《安和之曲》：一誠盡兮予心懌，五福降兮民獲禧。

translations.literal: Removing the feast, "Secure Harmony": one sincerity exhausted — my heart is pleased; five blessings descend — the people gain auspiciousness.
translations.idiomatic: Removing the feast — "Secure Harmony": our single sincerity is spent and my heart is pleased; five blessings descend and the people receive joy.

sentences.zh: 仰九光兮誠已申，終三獻兮徹敢遲。

translations.literal: Looking up to the nine lights — sincerity already expressed; ending three offerings — dare we delay in withdrawing?
translations.idiomatic: We look up to the nine lights, sincerity expressed; the three offerings ended — who would dare delay withdrawal?

sentences.zh: 送神，《昭和之曲》：祀禮既周兮樂舞揚，神享以納兮還青鄉。

translations.literal: Sending off the Spirit, "Bright Harmony": the sacrificial rite is already complete — music and dance rise; the spirit enjoys and accepts, returning to the azure realm.
translations.idiomatic: Sending off the Spirit — "Bright Harmony": the sacrifice is complete, music and dance ascend; the spirit accepts and returns to the azure realm.

sentences.zh: 予當拜首兮奉送，願恩光兮普萬方。

translations.literal: I should bow head to ground in sending off; we wish grace-light would spread to the ten thousand regions.
translations.idiomatic: I bow my head in farewell; we pray grace-light may reach every quarter.

sentences.zh: 永耀熹明兮攸賴，烝民鹹仰兮恩光。

translations.literal: Forever shining, bright and clear — thereby we rely; the multitude of people all look up to grace-light.
translations.idiomatic: Forever shining bright we rely upon You; all the people look up to Your radiant grace.

sentences.zh: 望燎之曲：睹六龍兮御駕，神變化兮鳳翥鸞翔。

translations.literal: Tune for gazing at the burning: we behold six dragons harnessing the ride; the spirit transforms — phoenix soars, luan flies.
translations.idiomatic: Tune for gazing at the burning: we behold six dragons guiding the carriage; the spirit transforms as phoenix and luan soar on high.

sentences.zh: 束帛餚羞兮詣燎方，佑我皇明兮基緒隆長。

translations.literal: Bundled silks and delicacies proceed to the burning place; protect our august brilliance — foundation and succession lofty and long.
translations.idiomatic: Bundled silks and delicacies proceed to the burning place; protect our bright dynasty, its foundation lofty and long.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年夕月樂章。

translations.literal: Music for the Evening Moon sacrifice, third year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Hymns for the Evening Moon sacrifice, Hongwu reign year 3.

sentences.zh: 周天星辰附。

translations.literal: The stars of the round Heaven are attached.
translations.idiomatic: The stars of the circuit of Heaven are included.

sentences.zh: 二十一年罷。

translations.literal: Abolished in the twenty-first year.
translations.idiomatic: Abolished in year 21.

sentences.zh: 迎神，《凝和之曲》：吉日良辰，祀典式陳。

translations.literal: Welcoming the Spirit, "Concentrated Harmony": an auspicious day, a fine hour — the sacrificial canon is formally set forth.
translations.idiomatic: Welcoming the Spirit — "Concentrated Harmony": on an auspicious day, at a propitious hour, the sacrificial canon is formally set forth.

sentences.zh: 太陰夜明，以及星辰。

translations.literal: Great Yin, night brilliance, and also the stars.
translations.idiomatic: Great Yin, night brilliance, and the stars as well.

sentences.zh: 濯濯厥靈，昭鑑我心以候以迎，來格來歆。

translations.literal: Bright and clear is its spirit; it brightly mirrors my heart — we wait and welcome; come near, come and enjoy.
translations.idiomatic: Bright and clear is its spirit; it mirrors our hearts as we wait and welcome; come near and accept our offering.

sentences.zh: 四年，星辰別祀，改「以及星辰。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, stars received separate sacrifice; changed the line "and also the stars."
translations.idiomatic: In year 4, the stars received a separate sacrifice; the line "and the stars as well" was changed.

sentences.zh: 」句爲「惟德孔神」。

translations.literal: The closing line was changed to "only virtue, the great spirit."
translations.idiomatic: The closing line was changed to "only virtue, the great spirit."

sentences.zh: 奠帛以下，鹹同朝日。

translations.literal: From offering silks downward, all are the same as the Morning Sun.
translations.idiomatic: From offering silks onward, the rite is the same as for the Morning Sun.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖九年復定夕月樂章。

translations.literal: Music for the Evening Moon sacrifice, re-fixed, ninth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: Hymns for the Evening Moon sacrifice, re-established, Jiajing reign year 9.

sentences.zh: 迎神，《凝和之曲》：陰曰配合兮承陽宗，式循古典兮齋以恭。

translations.literal: Welcoming the Spirit, "Concentrated Harmony": Yin is called the partner — receiving the Yang lineage; formally following ancient canon — fasting in reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Welcoming the Spirit — "Concentrated Harmony": Yin pairs with Yang in cosmic union; we follow the ancient canon, fasting in reverence.

sentences.zh: 睹太陰來格兮星辰羅從，予拜首兮迓神容。

translations.literal: We behold Great Yin come near — stars arrayed in following; I bow head to ground and welcome the spirit's countenance.
translations.idiomatic: We behold Great Yin draw near, stars arrayed in attendance; I bow my head and welcome the spirit's presence.

sentences.zh: 初獻，《壽和之曲》：神其來止，有嚴其誠。

translations.literal: First offering, "Longevity and Harmony": may the spirit come and halt; there is sternness in its sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: First offering — "Longevity and Harmony": may the spirit come and abide; our sincerity is solemn and strict.

sentences.zh: 玉帛在篚，清酤方盈。

translations.literal: Jade and silk are in the basket; clear brew is just full.
translations.idiomatic: Jade and silk rest in the basket; clear wine is freshly poured.

sentences.zh: 奉而奠之，願鑑微情。

translations.literal: We present and set them forth; we wish You would mirror our slight feeling.
translations.idiomatic: We present and set them forth; we pray You will regard our humble hearts.

sentences.zh: 夫祀兮云何？

translations.literal: This sacrifice — what is it for?
translations.idiomatic: What is this sacrifice for?

sentences.zh: 祈佑兮羣氓。

translations.literal: We pray for protection for the multitude of commoners.
translations.idiomatic: We pray for protection for all the people.

sentences.zh: 亞獻，《豫和之曲》：二觴載斟，樂舞雍雍。

translations.literal: Second offering, "Ease and Harmony": two goblets are borne and poured; music and dance are harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Second offering — "Ease and Harmony": two goblets are poured; music and dance proceed in harmony.

sentences.zh: 神歆且樂，百職惟供。

translations.literal: The spirit enjoys and is pleased; the hundred offices only supply.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit accepts and rejoices; the hundred offices attend.

sentences.zh: 願順軌兮五行，祈民福兮惟神必從。

translations.literal: We wish to follow the tracks of the Five Phases; we pray the people's blessing — only the spirit must follow.
translations.idiomatic: We pray the Five Phases may run in order; we pray blessing for the people — the spirit surely heeds.

sentences.zh: 終獻，《康和之曲》：一誠以申，三舉金觥。

translations.literal: Final offering, "Healthful Harmony": one sincerity thereby expressed; three times the golden goblet is raised.
translations.idiomatic: Final offering — "Healthful Harmony": one sincerity expressed; three times the golden goblet is raised.

sentences.zh: 鐘鼓鍧鍧，環珮琤琤。

translations.literal: Bells and drums boom and boom; ring-pendants tinkle and tinkle.
translations.idiomatic: Bells and drums resound; pendants ring clear.

sentences.zh: 鑑予之情，願永保我民生。

translations.literal: Mirror my feeling; we wish forever to protect our people's lives.
translations.idiomatic: Regard our hearts; we pray You will forever protect our people's lives.

sentences.zh: 徹饌，《安和之曲》：禮樂肅具，精意用申。

translations.literal: Removing the feast, "Secure Harmony": ritual and music are solemnly complete; refined intent is thereby expressed.
translations.idiomatic: Removing the feast — "Secure Harmony": ritual and music stand complete; refined intent is expressed.

sentences.zh: 位坎居歆，納茲藻蘋。

translations.literal: In the Kan position it dwells and enjoys; it receives these water plants and duckweed.
translations.idiomatic: Dwelling in the northern position it accepts; it receives these water plants and duckweed.

sentences.zh: 徹之弗遲，儀典肅陳。

translations.literal: Withdrawing without delay; ritual canon is solemnly set forth.
translations.idiomatic: We withdraw without delay; the ritual canon is solemnly observed.

sentences.zh: 神其鑑之，佑我生民。

translations.literal: May the spirit mirror this; protect our living people.
translations.idiomatic: May the spirit regard this and protect our people.

sentences.zh: 送神，《保和之曲》：禮備告終兮神喜旋，穹碧澄輝兮素華鮮。

translations.literal: Sending off the Spirit, "Preserving Harmony": the rite is prepared and announces its end — the spirit joyfully wheels back; azure sky is clear in radiance, plain splendor fresh.
translations.idiomatic: Sending off the Spirit — "Preserving Harmony": the rite is complete and the spirit joyfully returns; the azure sky shines clear, plain splendor fresh.

sentences.zh: 星辰從兮返神鄉，露氣清兮霓裳蹁躚。

translations.literal: Stars follow and return to the spirit realm; dew-vapor is clear — rainbow garments dance lightly.
translations.idiomatic: The stars follow and return to the spirit realm; dew is clear and rainbow garments dance lightly.

sentences.zh: 望瘞之曲：餚羞兮束帛，薦之於瘞兮罔敢愆。

translations.literal: Tune for gazing at the burial: delicacies and bundled silks; presenting them at the burial — we dare not err.
translations.idiomatic: Tune for gazing at the burial: delicacies and bundled silks; we present them at the burial, daring not to err.

sentences.zh: 予拜首兮奉送，願永貺兮民樂豐年。

translations.literal: I bow head to ground in sending off; we wish eternal bestowal — the people rejoice in abundant years.
translations.idiomatic: I bow my head in farewell; we pray for lasting blessing and abundant years for the people.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十年，定祈谷樂章。

translations.literal: Tenth year of Jiajing — fixed the music for the Grain Prayer.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing reign year 10: hymns for the Grain Prayer were established.

sentences.zh: 迎神，《中和之曲》：臣惟穹昊兮民物之初，爲民請命兮祀禮昭諸。

translations.literal: Welcoming the Spirit, "Moderation and Harmony": the minister thinks only of the vast vault — beginning of people and things; for the people we petition fate — sacrificial rite made manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Welcoming the Spirit — "Moderation and Harmony": we think of the vast heavens, source of all people and things; we petition on the people's behalf and make the sacrifice manifest.

sentences.zh: 備筵率職兮祈洪庥，臣衷微眇兮悃懇誠攄。

translations.literal: Preparing the feast, leading duties — we pray for vast blessing; the minister's heart is slight and tiny — sincere feeling poured forth.
translations.idiomatic: We prepare the feast and lead our duties, praying for vast blessing; our humble hearts pour forth sincere devotion.

sentences.zh: 遙瞻駕降兮霽色輝，歡迎鼓舞兮迓龍輿。

translations.literal: Gazing from afar at the carriage descending — clear weather shines; welcome with drum and dance — greeting the dragon carriage.
translations.idiomatic: We gaze from afar as the carriage descends in clear radiance; we welcome with drum and dance, greeting the dragon carriage.

sentences.zh: 臣愧菲才兮後斯民，願福斯民兮聖恩渠。

translations.literal: The minister is ashamed of slight talent — behind these people; we wish blessing for these people — sage grace like a channel.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed of our slight talent, we stand behind the people; we pray blessing for them through the channel of sage grace.

sentences.zh: 奠玉帛，《肅和之曲》：烝民勤職兮農事顓，蠶工亦慎兮固桑阡。

translations.literal: Offering jade and silk, "Reverent Harmony": the multitude labor diligently — agricultural affairs are focused; silkworm work is also careful — securing mulberry paths.
translations.idiomatic: Offering jade and silk — "Reverent Harmony": the people labor diligently in farming; silkworm work is careful, mulberry paths secured.

sentences.zh: 玉帛祗奉兮暨豆籩，仰祈大化兮錫以豐年。

translations.literal: Jade and silk reverently presented — reaching trays and baskets; looking up we pray the great transformation — bestow abundant years.
translations.idiomatic: Jade and silk are reverently offered with trays and baskets; we pray the great transformation will grant abundant harvests.

sentences.zh: 進俎，《咸和之曲》：鼎烹兮氣馨，香羞兮旨醽。

translations.literal: Presenting the sacrifice tray, "All Harmony": tripod cooking — vapor fragrant; fragrant delicacies — rich brew sweet.
translations.idiomatic: Presenting the sacrifice tray — "All Harmony": the tripod cooks, fragrance rising; delicacies and rich wine are sweet.

sentences.zh: 帝垂享兮以歆，烝民蒙福兮以寧。

translations.literal: The Emperor lowers enjoyment and accepts; the multitude receive blessing and thereby peace.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor deigns to partake; the people receive blessing and dwell in peace.

sentences.zh: 初獻，《壽和之曲》：禮嚴兮初獻行，百職趨蹌兮佩琤鳴。

translations.literal: First offering, "Longevity and Harmony": the rite is stern — first offering proceeds; the hundred offices hurry in measured steps — pendants ring.
translations.idiomatic: First offering — "Longevity and Harmony": the rite is solemn as the first offering proceeds; the hundred offices hurry forward, pendants ringing.

sentences.zh: 臣謹進兮玉觥，帝心歆鑑兮歲豐亨。

translations.literal: The minister reverently advances the jade goblet; the Emperor's heart enjoys and mirrors — years abundant and prosperous.
translations.idiomatic: The minister reverently presents the jade goblet; the Emperor accepts and regards — the year is abundant and prosperous.

sentences.zh: 亞獻，《景和之曲》：二觴舉兮致虔，清醴載斟兮奉前。

translations.literal: Second offering, "Scenic Harmony": two goblets raised — utmost reverence shown; clear rich wine is poured and borne forward.
translations.idiomatic: Second offering — "Scenic Harmony": two goblets are raised in reverence; clear rich wine is poured and borne forward.

sentences.zh: 仰音容兮忻穆，臣感聖恩兮實拳拳。

translations.literal: Looking up at voice and countenance — joyful and solemn; the minister feels sage grace — truly earnest and sincere.
translations.idiomatic: We look up at His voice and countenance, joyful and solemn; the minister feels sage grace with earnest heart.

sentences.zh: 終獻，《永和之曲》：三獻兮一誠微，禋禮告成兮帝鑑是依。

translations.literal: Final offering, "Eternal Harmony": three offerings — one sincerity slight; the sacrificial rite announces completion — the Emperor's regard is what we rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Final offering — "Eternal Harmony": three offerings, one humble sincerity; the sacrifice is complete and we rely on the Emperor's regard.

sentences.zh: 烝民沐德兮歲豐禨，臣拜首兮竭誠祈。

translations.literal: The multitude bathe in virtue — years abundant and auspicious; the minister bows head to ground — exhausting sincerity in prayer.
translations.idiomatic: The people bathe in virtue, years abundant and auspicious; the minister bows his head and prays with utmost sincerity.

sentences.zh: 徹饌，《凝和之曲》：三獻周兮肅乃儀，俎豆敬徹兮弗敢遲。

translations.literal: Removing the feast, "Concentrated Harmony": three offerings complete — solemn is the ritual; trays and vessels reverently withdrawn — we dare not delay.
translations.idiomatic: Removing the feast — "Concentrated Harmony": three offerings complete, the ritual solemn; trays and vessels are reverently withdrawn without delay.

sentences.zh: 願留福兮丕而，曰雨曰暘兮若時。

translations.literal: We wish to leave blessing great and vast; saying rain, saying sunshine — as if in season.
translations.idiomatic: We pray blessing may remain, great and vast; rain and sunshine in their proper seasons.

sentences.zh: 送神，《清和之曲》：祀禮告備兮帝鑑彰，臣情上達兮感昊蒼。

translations.literal: Sending off the Spirit, "Clear Harmony": the sacrificial rite announces readiness — the Emperor's regard is manifest; the minister's feeling reaches above — feeling the vast azure.
translations.idiomatic: Sending off the Spirit — "Clear Harmony": the sacrifice is complete and the Emperor's regard shines forth; the minister's heart reaches above, moved by the vast heavens.

sentences.zh: 雲程肅駕兮返帝鄉，臣荷恩眷兮何以忘。

translations.literal: Cloud journey, solemn carriage — returning to the Emperor's realm; the minister bears favoring grace — how could we forget?
translations.idiomatic: The solemn carriage returns through clouds to the celestial realm; the minister bears favoring grace — how could we forget?

sentences.zh: 祥風瑞靄兮彌壇壝，烝民率土兮悉獲豐康。

translations.literal: Auspicious wind, lucky mist fill the altar mound; the multitude throughout the realm all gain abundance and peace.
translations.idiomatic: Auspicious wind and lucky mist fill the altar mound; the people throughout the realm all gain abundance and peace.

sentences.zh: 望燎，《太和之曲》：遙睹兮天衢長，邈彼寥廓兮去上方。

translations.literal: Gazing at the burning, "Supreme Harmony": gazing from afar — the heavenly road is long; far away that vast expanse — departing for the heights above.
translations.idiomatic: Gazing at the burning — "Supreme Harmony": we behold from afar the long heavenly road; far away the vast expanse, departing for the heights above.

sentences.zh: 束帛薦火兮升聞，悃愊通兮沛澤長。

translations.literal: Bundled silks offered to fire ascend and are heard; sincere feeling connects — vast moisture long.
translations.idiomatic: Bundled silks offered to the fire ascend and are heard; sincere feeling connects and grace flows long.

sentences.zh: 樂終九奏兮神人以和，臣同率土兮鹹荷恩光。

translations.literal: Music ends — nine performances; spirit and human are in harmony; the minister together with all within the realm all bear grace-light.
translations.idiomatic: Music ends with nine performances, spirit and human in harmony; the minister with all within the realm bears radiant grace.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十七年，定大饗樂章。

translations.literal: Seventeenth year of Jiajing — fixed the music for the Great Feast.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing reign year 17: hymns for the Great Feast were established.

sentences.zh: 迎神，《中和之曲》：於皇穆清兮弘覆惟仁，既成萬寶兮惠此烝民。
